title: Strict quotient reduction model and completion-unit normalization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, $A_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $T$ a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived category [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the completion reflector $C_T$ with unit $\eta_T$ onto the full derived-complete subcategory of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]; thus $C_TV=R\lim_n(V\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_T)$. Put $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and use the small diagram site of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Its constant ring sheaf is $\Delta\underline A_T$ and its quotient ring sheaf is $B_T=(\underline{A_n}_T)_n$ with the actual quotient transitions. A $B_T$-module system consists of module sheaves $M_n$ over $\underline{A_n}_T$ and $\underline{A_{n+1}}_T$-linear transition maps to $M_n$ by restriction of scalars. Write $\Delta$ for the constant-tower functor, $U_T$ for restriction to constant-$A$ towers, $S_T=-\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}B_T$, $\mathcal R_T=S_T\Delta$, $i_V:\Delta V\to U_T\mathcal R_TV$ for the quotient augmentation, and $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$ on constant-$A$ towers, with its canonical identification $\ell_V:\mathcal L_T\Delta V\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then: (1) the ring sheaf $B_T$ realizes the category of strict semilinear quotient systems, with componentwise kernels, cokernels and cohomology, and $U_T$ is exact and conservative on derived categories; (2) for every $V\in D_T$, a single flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to V$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution] gives a K-flat diagonal $\Delta Q$ and represents $\mathcal R_TV$ by the strict complex $(Q\otimes_A\underline{A_n}_T)_n$ with quotient transitions, and under this identification $i_V$ is represented by the termwise quotient maps; (3) the constant-tower functor $\Delta$ preserves K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and on a K-injective $V$ the map $\ell_V$ is represented by the literal equality $\lim\Delta V=V$; (4) $\mathcal L_TU_T\mathcal R_T=C_T$ canonically, and $\mathcal L_T(i_V)\ell_V^{-1}=\eta_{T,V}$. These are identities of natural transformations in $V$.

proof.text: Use the sheaf equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] for $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. The diagram of quotient ring sheaves gives $B(n,U)=\underline{A_n}_T(U)$ on this site: its restrictions in the index direction are the actual quotient maps. The sheaf condition is vertical, hence holds because each $\underline{A_n}_T$ is a sheaf. Unpack [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] for this ring. Restriction to the $n$th slice gives an $\underline{A_n}_T$-module $M_n$; the horizontal restrictions give exactly the required semilinear transitions. Conversely these data define $M(n,U)=M_n(U)$, with restriction along a horizontal-vertical composite the composite of the supplied transition and vertical restriction. Their commuting square and cocycle give the functor laws. These constructions are inverse on objects and maps. Restricting along $\Delta\underline A_T\to B$ leaves all section groups and transitions unchanged, as in [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), sequence site; sites-modules.tex Tags 03CW (definition-sheaf-modules) and 03CS (restriction of scalars). Explicit varying-ring unpacking of the product-site equivalence.

proof.text: Sheafification on the vertical site is componentwise. Indeed, sheafify each slice of a presheaf module using [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]; each transition extends uniquely to these sheafifications. Uniqueness gives all transition identities. Maps from this system to any sheaf system correspond, slice by slice, to maps from the original presheaf system, so this is the sheafification universal property. Now [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] computes a sheaf tensor by sheafifying sectionwise tensors. Its $n$th slice is therefore the ordinary tensor on $T$, with transition on pure tensors $x\otimes y\mapsto t(x)\otimes t(y)$. Direct sums are componentwise as well: maps out of their componentwise sums are precisely families of system maps out of the summands. Consequently evaluation commutes with the direct-sum total tensor and its signed differential in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. These identifications send all local pure tensors to themselves.

source.place: Tags 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules) and 03EK (section-tensor-product); vertical-site universal-property calculation; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YL (section-flat).

proof.text: For a system map $f:M\to N$, [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] gives its kernel as sectionwise kernels and its cokernel as the sheafification of sectionwise cokernels. Step 2 makes these precisely $(\ker f_n)_n$ and $(\operatorname{coker}f_n)_n$ with the induced semilinear transitions. Thus cohomology is componentwise. Restriction $U$ preserves these objects and is exact. It reflects isomorphisms of module sheaves: the inverse of a bijective underlying module map is module-linear, and the component inverses commute with the transitions. Exactness of constant-ring tower evaluation is also [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], $U$ and $\Delta$ induce exact derived functors represented termwise.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian), followed by homology.tex Tag 02MZ (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian); derived.tex localization of an exact functor.

proof.text: The derived $U$ is conservative, not merely conservative on strict maps. By [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system] and [lem-pc-left-localization-fraction-representation], write any derived morphism as $\alpha=[s]^{-1}[f]$ with $s:Y\to Z$ a quasi-isomorphism and $f:X\to Z$ a map of complexes. If $U\alpha$ is invertible, then $[Uf]$ is invertible. Applying the cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes every $H^q(Uf)=U(H^q f)$ invertible. The abelian conservativity from Step 3 makes every $H^q f$ invertible. Hence $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $\alpha$ is invertible. This proves clause (1) on the ordinary unbounded derived categories.

source.place: Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic), calculus of fractions; categories.tex Tag 04VE (lemma-morphisms-left-localization).

proof.text: Choose a single flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to V$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The diagonal is K-flat on the constant-ring diagram site: for every acyclic tower complex $E$, Step 3 makes each $E_n$ acyclic, while Step 2 identifies $(E\otimes\Delta Q)_n$ with $E_n\otimes Q$. Each is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex], so the tower tensor is acyclic. Its terms are flat too: tensoring with $\Delta Q^q$ is componentwise tensoring with the flat sheaf $Q^q$ and thus preserves short exact sequences. Moreover $\Delta Q\to\Delta V$ is a quasi-isomorphism by componentwise cohomology. This checks the resolving representative on the whole diagram site, rather than choosing unrelated representatives at different levels.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution) and 06YN (definition-K-flat), applied using the componentwise calculations in Steps 2-3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on the small diagram site to $\Delta\underline A_T\to B_T$ and the K-flat representative $\Delta Q$. It represents $S_T\Delta V$ by $(\Delta Q)\otimes_{\Delta\underline A_T}B_T$. Step 2 identifies this complex with $X_Q=(Q\otimes_A\underline{A_n}_T)_n$, with transitions $1_Q\otimes(\underline{A_{n+1}}_T\to\underline{A_n}_T)$. The quotient augmentation is the natural chain map $i_Q:\Delta Q\to UX_Q$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. The compatibility equation is $(1\otimes q_{n+1,n})(x\otimes1)=x\otimes1$; hence this is a strict map of towers, and localization gives $i_V$. Quasi-isomorphism invariance between K-flat representatives, including its canonical comparison, is part (1)-(2) of the cited change-of-rings theorem. This proves clause (2).

source.place: Tags 06YT (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side) and 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), for identity geometric morphism and change of rings.

proof.text: For completeness, the preservation assertion in clause (3) is an explicit null-homotopy calculation. If $E$ is an acyclic tower complex and $f:E\to\Delta J$ a chain map with $J$ K-injective, then $f_n=f_1p_{n1}$, where $p_{n1}:E_n\to E_1$ is the transition composite (identity for $n=1$). Componentwise exactness makes $E_1$ acyclic. By [def-pur-kinjective-complex], choose $h^q:E_1^q\to J^{q-1}$ with $f_1=dh+hd$. Set $h_n^q=h^q p_{n1}^q$. The equations $p_{n1}=p_{m1}p_{nm}$ for $n\ge m$ show this is a tower homotopy, and $dh_n+h_nd=(dh+hd)p_{n1}=f_n$. Thus $\Delta J$ is K-injective. Equivalently, $\operatorname{ev}_1\dashv\Delta$, the adjunction given by $f\mapsto f_1$ and $g\mapsto(gp_{n1})_n$, has exact left adjoint.

source.place: Tag 070H (definition-K-injective); explicit instance of Tag 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives), with the adjunction and null-homotopy written out.

proof.text: For any complex $J$, $J$ with identity projections is the literal limit of $\Delta J$: a compatible family of maps to $J$ has all its components equal, since every pair of levels has a common higher level. Thus the limit cone is represented by $J$ itself. Choose a K-injective representative $V\to J$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Step 7 and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] compute $\mathcal L_T\Delta V$ by $\lim\Delta J=J$. The resulting $\ell_V$ is the identity on this representative. Its inverse is the canonical constant-cone map. These identifications are natural on K-injective representatives, and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies every derived map between such representatives with its homotopy class. Hence $\ell$ is a canonical natural isomorphism on $D_T$, proving clause (3).

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits) and Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); injectives.tex Tag 079P (theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck); derived.tex Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective).

proof.text: By Step 6, $U_T\mathcal R_TV$ is one strict tower presenting all the derived tensors $V\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_T$, with their actual quotient transitions. Its total derived limit is the functor of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction], namely the completion reflector $C_T$. This yields the canonical comparison $\mathcal L_TU_T\mathcal R_T\cong C_T$, interpreted with the full-subcategory inclusion when necessary. Both sides use the same strict quotient complex $UX_Q$ and the same total right derived inverse limit of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]; this comparison does not replace a strict tower by an independently chosen diagram in $D_T$.

proof.text: Identify the entire augmented map on a representative. Write $a:UX_Q\to I$ for a K-injective tower resolution and $j:Q\to J$ for a K-injective resolution, supplied by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The map $ai_Q:\Delta Q\to I$ corresponds to a chain map $k:Q\to\lim I$ with projections $k_n=a_n(x\mapsto x\otimes1)$. Because $\Delta J$ and $I$ are K-injective, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents $[ai_Q][\Delta j]^{-1}$ by a chain map $b:\Delta J\to I$, with $b\Delta j$ homotopic to $ai_Q$. Taking the literal limit carries a tower homotopy to a homotopy (apply the limit to its degree maps). Since $\lim\Delta J=J$, this says $(\lim b)j$ is homotopic to $k$. The derived-limit computation of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] therefore identifies $[k]$ with $\mathcal L_T(i_V)\ell_V^{-1}$, after the comparison $[Q]\cong V$. This verifies a derived morphism, rather than only its projections after evaluation.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), total derived inverse limit computed on K-injectives; derived.tex Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), full faithfulness on morphisms into K-injectives. Explicit augmentation calculation.

proof.text: Since $A$ is Noetherian, choose finitely many generators of $I$ using [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] with coefficient sheaf $\underline A_T$. Its final paragraph identifies Koszul completion with the quotient-tower completion, respecting the units: the canonical quotient-tower map is the completion unit. On $Q$ that canonical map is precisely the augmentation $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ into the quotient system, followed by its K-injective total-limit comparison; Step 10 computes it as $[k]$. Under the reflector identification of Step 9 it is therefore $\eta_{T,V}$, giving $\mathcal L_T(i_V)\ell_V^{-1}=\eta_{T,V}$. For a chain map $c:Q\to Q'$ the strict equation $(c\otimes1)(x\otimes1)=c(x)\otimes1$ proves the naturality square before taking derived limits. The canonical K-flat comparisons of Step 6 and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descend this square and the comparison of Step 9 to every derived morphism. Thus clause (4) and its natural-transformation assertion hold.
